title: App Registrations and Service Principals
description: Learn how to register an application in Entra ID and understand the difference between an app registration and a service principal.

data.text: An app registration is a blueprint — it defines your app's identity, redirect URIs, and the permissions it needs. A service principal is the local identity your app uses at runtime in a specific tenant.

cards.title: App Registration
cards.description: The global definition of your application in Entra ID.

cards.title: Service Principal
cards.description: The security principal used by your app in one tenant.

data.title: Create an App Registration with Azure CLI
data.content: Register a new application in Entra ID using the Azure CLI. This creates the app registration.

data.title: Create a Service Principal with Azure CLI
data.content: After registering the app, create a service principal so the app can sign in and get tokens.

data.text: An app registration creates an application object in your tenant. That object is the definition: display name, redirect URIs, client ID, API permissions, exposed scopes, and app roles. A service principal is the local representation of an application in one tenant. It is the thing you assign roles to and the thing that actually authenticates. One application object can have service principals in many tenants: your own, plus one per customer tenant for a multi-tenant app.

rows: Client ID, redirect URIs, permissions, secrets

data.title: Create a registration, service principal, and secret
data.content: A scripted equivalent of the portal flow. Capture the app ID once and reuse it.
data.code:
appId=$(az ad app create --display-name "orders-api" --sign-in-audience AzureADMyOrg --query appId -o tsv)

# Create the service principal in the current tenant
az ad sp create --id "$appId"

# Create a client secret valid for one year (store it in Key Vault, never in Git)
az ad app credential reset --id "$appId" --years 1 --query "{clientId:appId, secret:password}" -o json

# Add a delegated permission, for example Microsoft Graph User.Read
az ad app permission add --id "$appId" \
  --api 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 \
  --api-permissions e1fe6dd8-ba31-4d61-89e7-88639da4683d=Scope

data.text: A client secret is a password with an expiry date. Federated identity credentials remove it. The external platform (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Kubernetes) issues a short-lived OIDC token that Entra ID exchanges for an access token, trusting a specific issuer, subject, and audience. Nothing long-lived is stored.

data.title: Trust a GitHub Actions workflow with OIDC
data.content: The subject must match the repository and branch or environment exactly. Put the JSON in a file so quoting does not get in the way.
data.code:
# federated-credential.json
# {
#   "name": "github-main",
#   "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
#   "subject": "repo:my-org/my-repo:ref:refs/heads/main",
#   "audiences": ["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]
# }

az ad app federated-credential create \
  --id "$appId" \
  --parameters @federated-credential.json

data.title: Secrets expire silently
data.text: A client secret that expires at 2 a.m. will break production at 2 a.m. If you must use one, store it in Key Vault, set an expiry you monitor, and automate rotation. Federated credentials avoid the problem entirely.

data.title: Practice: Register a Demo App
data.description: In the Azure Portal, navigate to Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Name it 'demo-api', set redirect URI to 'https://jwt.ms', and save the Application (client) ID.
steps: Open Azure Portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID.
Click Register and copy the Application (client) ID.
data.expectedOutcome: You will have a new app registration and be able to see its client ID in the overview pane.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: An app registration defines what your app is.
A service principal is what your app uses in a tenant to authenticate.
One app registration can have many service principals across tenants.
